# @k8ordo/color-scheme

> The colour-scheme axis of an application, owned. The visitor's preference
> — light, dark, or nothing, which follows the default (the system unless
> told otherwise) — lives in localStorage through `@k8ordo/state`; one rule
> resolves it against `prefers-color-scheme`; the result is the `dark` class
> on `<html>` (what `@k8ordo/ui` reads, and Tailwind's `dark:` with a
> class-based `@custom-variant dark`). `<ColorSchemeScript>` in the root
> layout's `<head>` is the inline script that puts the class on before the
> first paint, and `<ColorSchemeProvider>` in its `<body>` keeps it in step
> afterwards; `useColorScheme()` reads it. The server renders the default
> (`light` when that default is `'system'`).
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

When installed via npm, these docs live under `node_modules/@k8ordo/color-scheme/docs/`.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](GUIDE.md): what the package owns and does not (the class,
  not the colours or the `color-scheme` property; the rule, not the storage;
  no contrast preference — `prefers-contrast` and `forced-colors` are the
  OS's, which `@k8ordo/ui` follows in either scheme), placing the script in
  the root layout's `<head>` (ahead of every stylesheet, which
  `@k8ordo/framework` ensures) and the provider in its `<body>`, allowing
  the inline script under a Content-Security-Policy (by nonce or by hash,
  and what a blocked script costs), reading and changing the preference
  with the hook, the stored row and reading it without the hook, what it
  guarantees, and testing.

## Entry point

- `@k8ordo/color-scheme` — `<ColorSchemeScript defaultPreference? nonce?>`
  (goes in the root layout's `<head>`, ahead of every stylesheet, which
  `@k8ordo/framework` ensures) is the inline `<script>` that puts `dark` on
  `<html>` before the first paint from the stored preference, the default
  (`'system'` unless told otherwise), or the system; `nonce` signs it for a
  Content-Security-Policy (in `@k8ordo/framework`'s server mode, `nonce()`
  from `@k8ordo/framework/server`).
  `<ColorSchemeProvider defaultPreference?>` (client; goes inside `<body>`
  around everything) keeps the class in step after hydration; give it the
  same `defaultPreference` as the script.
  `colorSchemeScriptHash(defaultPreference?)` resolves to the script's hash
  as a CSP source (`'sha256-…'`), for a policy that allows it by hash —
  the `csp` option of `@k8ordo/framework`'s static mode. `useColorScheme()` returns
  `{ scheme, preference, setPreference }`: `scheme` is `'light' | 'dark'`
  on screen, `preference` is `'light' | 'dark' | 'system'`, and
  `setPreference('system')` clears the stored preference, so the default
  applies again. `colorSchemeState` is the `@k8ordo/state` local definition
  itself (`k8ordo-state:color-scheme`).
  Types: `ColorScheme`, `ColorSchemePreference`, `ColorSchemeProviderProps`,
  `ColorSchemeScriptProps`, `UseColorScheme`.
